top_choice_rationale: The Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall prediction, confirmed by helical edge transport in HgTe quantum wells, form a two-decade-old prediction-plus-experiment chain that changed how band insulators are classified and computed, and is distinct from the 2016 award on topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall state. The credit boundary (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan) is a real weakness, so I rank the magic-angle graphene prize (three names including Bistritzer) second and the lattice clock third; all three are better than no award.
